ledger.note: 1561: the archbishop's rule over Riga ends. The Riga page gives 1561 with the Livonian Order's demise and says Riga 'for twenty years had the status of a free imperial city'; the Livonian Confederation page says that 'the following year, Riga became a free imperial city after the last Archbishop of Riga, William of Brandenburg, lost government of the territory'. The Livonian War page is silent on both. 1561 is used (confidence 2) because the Riga page's twenty years end at 1581.

notes: City state of about twenty years (free imperial city). Riga was a Hanseatic member from 1282 (Riga page) and the archbishops ruled it until 1561 (Archbishopric of Riga page); the free-city years 1561-1581 are the only ones drawn as a separate state. The Riga page's infobox lists the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth from 1582 and the Swedish Empire from 1629 (Riga fell to Gustavus Adolphus in 1621); those transfers belong to the polish-lithuanian-commonwealth, swedish-livonia and russian dossiers. The extent is the Riga municipality as a stand-in for the city's land; the pages give none. Review eu-14-x (2026-10-31): the region {admin1: Riga, country: Latvia} resolved to the whole Riga planning region (30 municipalities, about 13,150 km2), not the city; replaced by a circle round the city (8 km for the city, 10 km where Daugavgriva is included).
